`gh layer10 digest` is implemented and committed on this branch in four commits; #10 stays CLOSED and now carries a comment naming them.

## What was built

`internal/digest/` — `query.go` (the two GraphQL searches and their decoding), `classify.go` (§9.2's predicates as pure functions over a snapshot), `render.go` (§9.5's escaping, §9.6's footer), `digest.go` (fetch orchestration and the counts) — plus `internal/cmd/digest.go`, a read-path transport seam on `Env`, and `gh.Client.CurrentRepository`. §4.13's phrase list is now exported from `internal/check` as `AssumedLine`/`UndecidedAssumed` and used by both the checker and the read path, so the two cannot come to disagree.

Three implementation points, each a way this could have looked right and been wrong:

- **The union branch.** `Context.Failing()` tests `conclusion` on `CheckRun` and `state` on `StatusContext`. Mutating it to read `conclusion` on both makes `TestStatusContextFailureIsBlocked` report `[4]` rather than `[1 3 4]`.
- **The re-query** runs for open pull requests only — a merged one returns `UNKNOWN` on every query — and anything still unknown lands in Unclassified with `mergeability not yet computed`, never in not-matched.
- **All three *Needs a decision* disjuncts**, including the fingerprint match against `NOT_PLANNED` issues, which is fetched as a third arm of the issue query's disjunction and is deliberately not scoped by the window.

## Verification, all run

`test -f internal/digest/digest_test.go` → exit 0. Both `-run` lines from the issue → `ok`, and `-v` confirms each named test actually exists. `go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./... -count=1` → all packages ok. `gofmt -l .` → nothing. Each of the three predicates above was mutation-tested: removing the branch fails the test that covers it, and the tree was restored.

**Live** (read-only): against `Xapicc/gh-layer10`, 13 considered / 12 Changed / 1 Needs a decision (#11) / 0 Blocked / 0 Unclassified / `HEAD 8f2ce1a` / 3 requests — matching `gh issue list --state all` exactly, and `--verbose` shows three `gh api graphql --paginate` invocations. Against `cli/cli --since 3d`: 18 Blocked with real `conflicting` / `N checks failing` / `changes requested` clauses, and `incomplete: the issue query reported 2097 results and returned 1000`.

Two things to flag. First, *Needs a decision* fired on #11 through `## Open decision`, not through `Assumed:` — the brief expected the reverse, but §14 item 7 records that the five bodies were rewritten, #11 now carries a real `## Open decision`, and its `Assumed:` line is a stated premise that §4.13's heuristic correctly declines (cross-checked: `check` passes `issue.confidence.undecided` on it). The `Assumed:` disjunct is covered by fixtures, not by live data, because #11 is the only open artefact here. Second, `cli/cli` shows the search's 1,000-result ceiling; the digest detects it by comparing `issueCount` against what arrived and says so on stderr and after the footer, but it is genuinely incomplete on repositories that large — recorded in §9.7 with why the alternative costs a request per object type without removing the ceiling.

I edited `docs/SPEC.md`: §14 gains item 10 (§9.2's Unclassified clause and §9.6's footer contradicted each other), §9.2's clause is corrected, and §9.7 gains the measured query facts. `Readme.md` untouched; nothing pushed, merged or rebased; no issue reopened or closed.

DONE

@@ -0,0 +1,121 @@
+package cmd
+
+import (
+	"flag"
+	"time"
+
+	"github.com/Xapicc/gh-layer10/internal/digest"
+	"github.com/Xapicc/gh-layer10/internal/gh"
+)
+
+// Reader is everything `gh layer10 digest` asks of GitHub (§9.7): one paginated
+// GraphQL call, the running request count §9.6's footer states, and the
+// repository gh resolves when --repo was not given.
+//
+// It is separate from Transport, which is the write path's, because the two ask
+// for different things — `gh api graphql --paginate` against named commands —
+// and one interface holding both would make every fake of either implement the
+// other.
+type Reader interface {
+	digest.Transport
+	CurrentRepository() (string, error)
+}
+
+// digestOptions is §11.4's command line. --json is a global flag (§11) and is
+// not repeated here.
+type digestOptions struct {
+	since        string
+	staleReview  string
+	markdown     bool
+	explainDrops bool
+}
+
+func newDigestCommand() *Command {
+	opts := &digestOptions{}
+	return &Command{
+		Name:     "digest",
+		Synopsis: "read a repository into §9's four sections, and state what was not rendered",
+		Usage:    "[--since DURATION] [--stale-review DURATION] [--markdown|--json] [--explain-drops]",
+		Flags: func(fs *flag.FlagSet) {
+			fs.StringVar(&opts.since, "since", "7d", "the window `DURATION` Changed is decided over")
+			fs.StringVar(&opts.staleReview, "stale-review", "3d", "how long `DURATION` a review request stands before it needs a human (§9.2)")
+			fs.BoolVar(&opts.markdown, "markdown", false, "render the digest as Markdown rather than as lines")
+			fs.BoolVar(&opts.explainDrops, "explain-drops", false, "list every not-matched artefact with the predicates that returned false")
+		},
+		Run: func(env *Env, args []string) error { return runDigest(env, opts, args) },
+	}
+}
+
+// runDigest is §11.4. It reads and writes nothing to GitHub, and it has no
+// failure exit code of its own: exit 0 even when every section is empty, because
+// "the repository is in a bad state" is not a failure of the digest, and exit 4
+// when the transport could not answer.
+func runDigest(env *Env, opts *digestOptions, args []string) error {
+	if len(args) > 0 {
+		return UsageErrorf("digest reads a repository, not a file; got %q", args[0])
+	}
+	if opts.markdown && env.Globals.JSON {
+		return UsageErrorf("--markdown and --json are alternatives (§11.4); pick one")
+	}
+	since, err := digest.ParseDuration(opts.since)
+	if err != nil {
+		return UsageErrorf("--since: %s", err)
+	}
+	staleReview, err := digest.ParseDuration(opts.staleReview)
+	if err != nil {
+		return UsageErrorf("--stale-review: %s", err)
+	}
+
+	reader, err := env.reader()
+	if err != nil {
+		return classifyTransport(err)
+	}
+	// §11's --repo defaults to "the current repository as gh resolves it", and the
+	// read path is the one command that cannot leave that resolution to gh: `gh
+	// api graphql` takes no --repo and substitutes nothing into a variable, so the
+	// repository has to be written into the search string. With --repo the answer
+	// is already here; without it, one request, counted in the footer like any
+	// other.
+	repository := env.Globals.Repo
+	if repository == "" {
+		if repository, err = reader.CurrentRepository(); err != nil {
+			return classifyTransport(err)
+		}
+	}
+
+	result, err := digest.Run(reader, digest.Options{
+		Repository:   repository,
+		Since:        since,
+		Window:       opts.since,
+		StaleReview:  staleReview,
+		Now:          time.Now(),
+		ExplainDrops: opts.explainDrops,
+		Warn:         env.Out.Warn,
+	})
+	if err != nil {
+		return classifyTransport(err)
+	}
+
+	if env.Globals.JSON {
+		return env.Out.ResultJSON(result)
+	}
+	if opts.markdown {
+		env.Out.Result("%s", result.Markdown())
+		return nil
+	}
+	env.Out.Result("%s", result.Text())
+	return nil
+}
+
+// reader builds the read path's transport, at the point the command needs one.
+//
+// Later than the command for the reason §3.5 keeps the codes apart, and behind
+// the same injectable seam as the write path's so that §9.2's predicates and
+// §9.7's request count are decidable in a test against a faked GraphQL rather
+// than against whatever this repository's issue list happens to hold today.
+func (e *Env) reader() (Reader, error) {
+	if e.newReader != nil {
+		return e.newReader(e)
+	}
+	return gh.New(gh.Options{Repo: e.Globals.Repo, Verbose: e.Out.Verbose})
+}

+	"flag"
+	"strings"
+	"testing"
+
+	"github.com/Xapicc/gh-layer10/internal/gh"
+)
+
+// `gh layer10 digest` end to end, against an injected reader (§11.4).
+//
+// The predicates themselves are internal/digest's to test — this is the command:
+// which flags are refused before a request is spent, what reaches stdout under
+// each rendering, and that the repository is resolved only when --repo did not
+// say.
+
+type fakeReader struct {
+	t *testing.T
+	// forbidden fails the test on any call. §11.4 has usage errors that must be
+	// decided from the command line alone, and a flag refused after a request was
+	// spent is a flag refused against §9.7's budget.
+	forbidden bool
+	repo      string
+	repoCalls int
+	queries   []string
+	requests  int
+	issues    string
+}
+
+func (f *fakeReader) Requests() int { return f.requests }
+
+func (f *fakeReader) CurrentRepository() (string, error) {
+	f.t.Helper()
+	if f.forbidden {
+		f.t.Fatal("the transport was reached; this command line is a usage error and §9.7's budget is shared")
+	}
+	f.repoCalls++
+	f.requests++
+	return "Xapicc/gh-layer10", nil
+}
+
+func (f *fakeReader) GraphQL(query string, fields ...gh.Field) ([]gh.Page, error) {
+	f.t.Helper()
+	if f.forbidden {
+		f.t.Fatal("the transport was reached; this command line is a usage error and §9.7's budget is shared")
+	}
+	f.requests++
+	switch {
+	case strings.Contains(query, `__type(name:`):
+		f.queries = append(f.queries, "introspect")
+		return page(`{"data":{"__type":{"enumValues":[{"name":"ISSUE_ADVANCED"}]}}}`), nil
+	case strings.Contains(query, "on PullRequest"):
+		f.queries = append(f.queries, "pr")
+		return page(`{"data":{"repository":{"nameWithOwner":"Xapicc/gh-layer10","defaultBranchRef":{"name":"main","target":{"oid":"8f2ce1a5ed1191eb677be5293a5e6f6f6ec0981e"}}},"search":{"issueCount":0,"pageInfo":{"hasNextPage":false},"nodes":[]}}}`), nil
+	case strings.Contains(query, "on Issue"):
+		f.queries = append(f.queries, "issue")
+		return page(`{"data":{"repository":{"nameWithOwner":"Xapicc/gh-layer10","defaultBranchRef":{"name":"main","target":{"oid":"8f2ce1a5ed1191eb677be5293a5e6f6f6ec0981e"}}},"search":{"issueCount":1,"pageInfo":{"hasNextPage":false},"nodes":[` + f.issueNodes() + `]}}}`), nil
+	}
+	f.t.Fatalf("the fake reader was sent a query it does not know:\n%s", query)
+	return nil, nil
+}
+
+func (f *fakeReader) issueNodes() string {
+	if f.issues != "" {
+		return f.issues
+	}
+	return `{"__typename":"Issue","number":11,"title":"Implementation order","url":"https://github.com/Xapicc/gh-layer10/issues/11","state":"OPEN","createdAt":"2026-08-15T21:53:33Z","author":{"login":"Xapicc"},"repository":{"nameWithOwner":"Xapicc/gh-layer10"},"body":"## Open decision\nWhether to split the query.\n"}`
+}
+
+func page(body string) []gh.Page {
+	return []gh.Page{{Headers: "HTTP/2.0 200 OK", Body: []byte(body)}}
+}
+
+func runDigestCLI(t *testing.T, reader *fakeReader, args ...string) result {
+	t.Helper()
+	reader.t = t
+	var out, errOut bytes.Buffer
+	code := execute(args, strings.NewReader(""), &out, &errOut, nil, func(*Env) (Reader, error) {
+		return reader, nil
+	})
+	return result{code: code, stdout: out.String(), stderr: errOut.String()}
+}
+
+func TestDigestPrintsFourSectionsAndAFooter(t *testing.T) {
+	reader := &fakeReader{}
+	got := runDigestCLI(t, reader, "digest", "--repo", "Xapicc/gh-layer10")
+
+	if got.code != exitOK {
+		t.Fatalf("§11.4 gives digest exit 0 on success, got %d: %s", got.code, got.stderr)
+	}
+	for _, want := range []string{"Changed (0)", "Blocked (0)", "Needs a decision (1)", "Unclassified (0)", "considered", "HEAD 8f2ce1a", "requests"} {
+		if !strings.Contains(got.stdout, want) {
+			t.Errorf("stdout is missing %q:\n%s", want, got.stdout)
+		}
+	}
+	if got.stderr != "" {
+		t.Errorf("§3.6: a conforming run writes nothing to stderr, got %q", got.stderr)
+	}
+	if reader.repoCalls != 0 {
+		t.Errorf("--repo said which repository; resolving it again spends a request for an answer we have, got %d", reader.repoCalls)
+	}
+}
+
+func TestDigestResolvesTheRepositoryOnlyWithoutRepo(t *testing.T) {
+	reader := &fakeReader{}
+	got := runDigestCLI(t, reader, "digest")
+
+	if got.code != exitOK {
+		t.Fatalf("exit %d: %s", got.code, got.stderr)
+	}
+	if reader.repoCalls != 1 {
+		t.Errorf("without --repo the repository has to be asked for once, got %d", reader.repoCalls)
+	}
+	if !strings.Contains(got.stdout, "· 4 requests") {
+		t.Errorf("the footer counts the resolution like any other request:\n%s", got.stdout)
+	}
+}
+
+func TestDigestJSONIsOneObject(t *testing.T) {
+	got := runDigestCLI(t, &fakeReader{}, "digest", "--repo", "Xapicc/gh-layer10", "--json")
+
+	if got.code != exitOK {
+		t.Fatalf("exit %d: %s", got.code, got.stderr)
+	}
+	if strings.Count(strings.TrimSpace(got.stdout), "\n") != 0 {
+		t.Fatalf("§3.6: a single JSON object and nothing else:\n%s", got.stdout)
+	}
+	var decoded struct {
+		Repository string `json:"repository"`
+		Sections   []struct {
+			Section string `json:"section"`
+			Count   int    `json:"count"`
+		} `json:"sections"`
+		Counts struct {
+			Considered int `json:"considered"`
+		} `json:"counts"`
+		Requests int `json:"requests"`
+	}
+	if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(got.stdout), &decoded); err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("cannot decode stdout as one object: %v\n%s", err, got.stdout)
+	}

+	}

+		t.Errorf("unexpected object: %+v", decoded)
+	}
+}

+func TestDigestMarkdownAndJSONAreAlternatives(t *testing.T) {

+func TestDigestMarkdownRendersHeadings(t *testing.T) {

+func TestDigestExplainDropsNamesPredicates(t *testing.T) {

+package digest
+
+import (
+	"encoding/json"
+	"fmt"
+	"strings"
+	"testing"
+	"time"
+
+	"github.com/Xapicc/gh-layer10/internal/gh"
+)
+
+// The fixture transport, and why the tests are written against one rather than
+// against this repository.
+//
+// §9.2 records three predicates that were false against the *API* while reading
+// as true in prose: a union type whose other half has no `conclusion`, a
+// three-valued enum whose third value is what a cold query returns, and a
+// section its own author never wrote. None of those is visible in a test that
+// asks GitHub what it thinks — the answer would be this repository's issue list
+// on the day the test ran, which has no conflicting pull request, no commit
+// status and no wontfix. So the responses are canned in the shape the API
+// returns, verified against api.github.com on 2026-08-16, and every predicate is
+// decided against them.
+
+// now is the instant every test is written against. A test that read the clock
+// would be a test whose window moved under it.
+var now = time.Date(2026, 8, 16, 12, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
+
+func at(offset time.Duration) time.Time { return now.Add(offset) }
+
+func stamp(t time.Time) string { return t.UTC().Format(time.RFC3339) }
+
+const (
+	testOwner = "Xapicc"
+	testName  = "gh-layer10"
+	testRepo  = testOwner + "/" + testName
+	testHead  = "8f2ce1a5ed1191eb677be5293a5e6f6f6ec0981e"
+)
+
+// fakeTransport answers the three query shapes this package sends. It keys off
+// the query text rather than off a call counter, so a test that reorders the
+// fetch still gets the right answer and a test asserting *how many* requests
+// were spent is asserting the thing §9.6's footer reports.
+type fakeTransport struct {
+	t *testing.T
+
+	defaultBranch string
+	head          string
+
+	// pulls and issues are the search nodes, in the shape the API returns them.
+	pulls  []map[string]any
+	issues []map[string]any
+
+	// pullPages and issuePages split the nodes across pages, as `--paginate`
+	// hands them over. Zero means one page.
+	pullPages  int
+	issuePages int
+
+	// reportedPulls and reportedIssues override issueCount, which is how the
+	// 1,000-result ceiling shows up: a count larger than the nodes returned.
+	reportedPulls  int
+	reportedIssues int
+
+	// requeried is what the mergeability re-query answers, and calls records
+	// every query so a test can assert it was asked once and no more.
+	requeried map[int]string
+	calls     []string
+
+	// legacyOnly drops ISSUE_ADVANCED from the introspection answer, which is the
+	// server this package refuses to guess against.
+	legacyOnly bool
+
+	requests int
+}
+
+func (f *fakeTransport) Requests() int { return f.requests }
+
+func (f *fakeTransport) GraphQL(query string, fields ...gh.Field) ([]gh.Page, error) {
+	f.t.Helper()
+	switch {
+	// `__type(name:` and not `SearchType`: both search queries declare
+	// `$type: SearchType!`, so a looser test here would answer every query with
+	// the introspection and the tests would pass against a fake that never
+	// searched anything.
+	case strings.Contains(query, `__type(name:`):
+		f.calls = append(f.calls, "introspect")
+		f.requests++
+		return f.pages([]string{f.introspection()}), nil
+	case strings.Contains(query, "on PullRequest"):
+		f.calls = append(f.calls, "search:pr")
+		return f.searchPages(f.pulls, f.pullPages, f.reportedPulls), nil
+	case strings.Contains(query, "on Issue"):
+		f.calls = append(f.calls, "search:issue")
+		return f.searchPages(f.issues, f.issuePages, f.reportedIssues), nil
+	case strings.Contains(query, "pullRequest(number:"):
+		f.calls = append(f.calls, "requery")
+		f.requests++
+		return f.pages([]string{f.mergeability(query)}), nil
+	}
+	f.t.Fatalf("the fake transport was sent a query it does not know:\n%s", query)
+	return nil, nil
+}
+
+func (f *fakeTransport) introspection() string {
+	values := []string{`{"name":"ISSUE"}`, `{"name":"REPOSITORY"}`}
+	if !f.legacyOnly {
+		values = append(values, `{"name":"ISSUE_ADVANCED"}`)
+	}
+	return `{"data":{"__type":{"enumValues":[` + strings.Join(values, ",") + `]}}}`
+}
+
+// mergeability answers only for the numbers the query actually asked about, so
+// a test cannot pass because the fake volunteered a pull request the re-query
+// never selected.
+func (f *fakeTransport) mergeability(query string) string {
+	selections := []string{}
+	for _, line := range strings.Split(query, "\n") {
+		var alias, number int
+		if _, err := fmt.Sscanf(strings.TrimSpace(line), "pr%d: pullRequest(number: %d)", &alias, &number); err != nil {
+			continue
+		}
+		state, ok := f.requeried[number]
+		if !ok {
+			state = mergeableUnknown
+		}
+		selections = append(selections, fmt.Sprintf(`"pr%d":{"number":%d,"mergeable":%q}`, number, number, state))
+	}
+	return `{"data":{"repository":{` + strings.Join(selections, ",") + `}}}`
+}
+
+func (f *fakeTransport) searchPages(nodes []map[string]any, pages, reported int) []gh.Page {
+	f.t.Helper()
+	if pages < 1 {
+		pages = 1
+	}
+	if reported == 0 {
+		reported = len(nodes)
+	}
+	size := (len(nodes) + pages - 1) / pages
+	var bodies []string
+	for page := 0; page < pages; page++ {
+		start := page * size
+		end := min(start+size, len(nodes))
+		if start > len(nodes) {
+			start = len(nodes)
+		}
+		var chunk []map[string]any
+		if start < end {
+			chunk = nodes[start:end]
+		}
+		encoded, err := json.Marshal(chunk)
+		if err != nil {
+			f.t.Fatalf("cannot encode the fixture nodes: %v", err)
+		}
+		if chunk == nil {
+			encoded = []byte("[]")
+		}
+		bodies = append(bodies, fmt.Sprintf(
+			`{"data":{"repository":{"nameWithOwner":%q,"defaultBranchRef":{"name":%q,"target":{"oid":%q}}},"search":{"issueCount":%d,"pageInfo":{"hasNextPage":%t,"endCursor":"c"},"nodes":%s}}}`,
+			testRepo, f.branch(), f.oid(), reported, page < pages-1, encoded))
+	}
+	// One request per page, which is what gh's --paginate spends and what
+	// internal/gh counts off the header blocks it wrote.
+	f.requests += len(bodies)
+	return f.pages(bodies)
+}
+
+func (f *fakeTransport) pages(bodies []string) []gh.Page {
+	out := make([]gh.Page, 0, len(bodies))
+	for _, body := range bodies {
+		out = append(out, gh.Page{Headers: "HTTP/2.0 200 OK", Body: []byte(body)})
+	}
+	return out
+}
+
+func (f *fakeTransport) branch() string {
+	if f.defaultBranch == "" {
+		return "main"
+	}
+	return f.defaultBranch
+}
+
+func (f *fakeTransport) oid() string {
+	if f.head == "" {
+		return testHead
+	}
+	return f.head
+}
+
+func (f *fakeTransport) calledTimes(call string) int {
+	n := 0
+	for _, made := range f.calls {
+		if made == call {
+			n++
+		}
+	}
+	return n
+}
+
+// pullNode is one search result in the shape the API returns a pull request,
+// with the fields every fixture would otherwise repeat filled in. Overrides win.
+func pullNode(number int, overrides map[string]any) map[string]any {
+	node := map[string]any{
+		"__typename":     "PullRequest",
+		"number":         number,
+		"title":          fmt.Sprintf("Pull request %d", number),
+		"url":            fmt.Sprintf("https://github.com/%s/pull/%d", testRepo, number),
+		"state":          "OPEN",
+		"body":           "",
+		"createdAt":      stamp(at(-24 * time.Hour)),
+		"baseRefName":    "main",
+		"mergeable":      "MERGEABLE",
+		"reviewDecision": "",
+		"author":         map[string]any{"login": "Xapicc"},
+		"repository":     map[string]any{"nameWithOwner": testRepo},
+	}
+	return apply(node, overrides)
+}
+
+func issueNode(number int, overrides map[string]any) map[string]any {
+	node := map[string]any{
+		"__typename": "Issue",
+		"number":     number,
+		"title":      fmt.Sprintf("Issue %d", number),
+		"url":        fmt.Sprintf("https://github.com/%s/issues/%d", testRepo, number),
+		"state":      "OPEN",
+		"body":       "",
+		"createdAt":  stamp(at(-24 * time.Hour)),
+		"author":     map[string]any{"login": "Xapicc"},
+		"repository": map[string]any{"nameWithOwner": testRepo},
+	}
+	return apply(node, overrides)
+}
+
+func apply(node, overrides map[string]any) map[string]any {
+	for key, value := range overrides {
+		node[key] = value
+	}
+	return node
+}
+
+// rollup wraps contexts the way the API nests them: commits(last:1) → commit →
+// statusCheckRollup → contexts. total defaults to the number given, and is set
+// higher by the test that asks what happens when the platform holds more
+// contexts than one request returns.
+func rollup(state string, total int, contexts ...map[string]any) map[string]any {
+	if total == 0 {
+		total = len(contexts)
+	}
+	if contexts == nil {
+		contexts = []map[string]any{}
+	}
+	return map[string]any{
+		"nodes": []any{map[string]any{
+			"commit": map[string]any{
+				"statusCheckRollup": map[string]any{
+					"state": state,
+					"contexts": map[string]any{
+						"totalCount": total,
+						"nodes":      contexts,
+					},
+				},
+			},
+		}},
+	}
+}
+
+// checkRun is the half of the union that has a `conclusion`.
+func checkRun(name, conclusion string) map[string]any {
+	return map[string]any{"__typename": "CheckRun", "name": name, "conclusion": conclusion}
+}
+
+// statusContext is the half that does not. The key is absent rather than empty,
+// exactly as the API omits it, so a predicate reading `conclusion` here reads a
+// field that is not in the response.
+func statusContext(context, state string) map[string]any {
+	return map[string]any{"__typename": "StatusContext", "context": context, "state": state}
+}
+
+func options(overrides func(*Options)) Options {
+	opts := Options{
+		Repository:  testRepo,
+		Since:       7 * 24 * time.Hour,
+		Window:      "7d",
+		StaleReview: 3 * 24 * time.Hour,
+		Now:         now,
+	}
+	if overrides != nil {
+		overrides(&opts)
+	}
+	return opts
+}
+
+func run(t *testing.T, transport *fakeTransport, overrides func(*Options)) Digest {
+	t.Helper()
+	transport.t = t
+	result, err := Run(transport, options(overrides))
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("Run: %v", err)
+	}
+	return result
+}
+
+// section returns one of §9.1's four by name, failing if it is absent — which is
+// itself the assertion of "exactly four, always printed".
+func section(t *testing.T, d Digest, name string) Section {
+	t.Helper()
+	for _, s := range d.Sections {
+		if s.Name == name {
+			return s
+		}
+	}
+	t.Fatalf("§9.1 requires the %q section to be printed always; the digest has %d sections", name, len(d.Sections))
+	return Section{}
+}
+
+func numbersIn(s Section) []int {
+	numbers := make([]int, 0, len(s.Items))
+	for _, item := range s.Items {
+		numbers = append(numbers, item.Number)
+	}
+	return numbers
+}
+
+func sameNumbers(got []int, want ...int) bool {
+	if len(got) != len(want) {
+		return false
+	}
+	for i := range got {
+		if got[i] != want[i] {
+			return false
+		}
+	}
+	return true
+}

+++ b/internal/digest/render.go
@@ -0,0 +1,180 @@
+package digest
+
+import (
+	"fmt"
+	"strings"
+	"unicode"
+)
+
+// titleLimit is §9.5's "truncated to 120 characters", counted in runes: a limit
+// counted in bytes would cut a multi-byte character in half and emit the halves.
+const titleLimit = 120
+
+// ellipsis marks a truncated string, and is counted inside the limit rather than
+// added to it. A digest that silently shortened a title would be lossy in a way
+// its reader could not see, which is the one kind of loss §9.4 does not allow.
+const ellipsis = "…"
+
+// markdownSpecial is the set escaped by renderText.
+//
+// It is the CommonMark punctuation that can change structure *in the middle of a
+// line*, which is the only position a title or a login is ever emitted in: the
+// backslash itself, code spans, emphasis, links, raw HTML and autolinks, table
+// cells and strikethrough. It is deliberately not every character CommonMark
+// permits a backslash before.
+//
+// `(` and `)` are not here, and that is the one judgement worth stating: a
+// parenthesis is only meaningful immediately after a `]`, and `]` is escaped —
+// so `[click](javascript:…)` cannot become a link either way, and escaping them
+// turned every ordinary title carrying a `(new)` marker into line noise. `#` and
+// `.` are absent for the same reason in the other direction: neither opens
+// anything except at the start of a line, and a title never starts one.
+const markdownSpecial = "\\`*_[]<>|~"
+
+// renderText is §9.5 applied to the only two untrusted strings in the output:
+// control characters stripped, truncated to 120 characters, Markdown specials
+// escaped. Everything else the digest prints is an identifier, a
+// platform-computed enumeration or a count.
+//
+// The order is deliberate and is not the order §9.5's sentence lists. Truncating
+// *after* escaping can cut a `\x` pair in half and emit the backslash alone,
+// which is a hard line break in Markdown and a dangling escape everywhere else.
+// So the title is stripped and truncated first — the 120-character bound is on
+// the title, which is what a reader is counting — and escaped last, which can
+// only lengthen the rendered form and can never leave an escape unfinished.
+func renderText(text string) string {
+	stripped := stripControl(text)
+	truncated := truncate(stripped, titleLimit)
+	return escapeMarkdown(truncated)
+}
+
+// stripControl removes every control character, newlines included. A title
+// carrying a newline would otherwise become two lines of a line-oriented format
+// and the second would read as an artefact nobody filed.
+func stripControl(text string) string {
+	var b strings.Builder
+	b.Grow(len(text))
+	for _, r := range text {
+		if unicode.IsControl(r) {
+			continue
+		}
+		b.WriteRune(r)
+	}
+	return b.String()
+}
+
+func truncate(text string, limit int) string {
+	runes := []rune(text)
+	if len(runes) <= limit {
+		return text
+	}
+	return string(runes[:limit-1]) + ellipsis
+}
+
+func escapeMarkdown(text string) string {
+	var b strings.Builder
+	b.Grow(len(text))
+	for _, r := range text {
+		if strings.ContainsRune(markdownSpecial, r) {
+			b.WriteByte('\\')
+		}
+		b.WriteRune(r)
+	}
+	return b.String()
+}
+
+// headShort is the seven-character form §9.6's footer prints.
+func headShort(oid string) string {
+	if oid == "" {
+		// A repository with no commits. Printing an empty field would read as a
+		// footer that forgot to say, and this says.
+		return "(none)"
+	}
+	if len(oid) <= 7 {
+		return oid
+	}
+	return oid[:7]
+}
+
+// Footer is §9.6, which is not optional. Without it the digest is a claim about
+// a repository with no statement of what it looked at, "which is exactly the
+// shape that lets a reader mistake 'nothing rendered' for 'nothing happened'".
+func (d Digest) Footer() string {
+	return fmt.Sprintf("%d considered · %d rendered · %d not matched · %d unclassified · window %s · HEAD %s · %d %s",
+		d.Counts.Considered, d.Counts.Rendered, d.Counts.NotMatched, d.Counts.Unclassified,
+		d.Window, headShort(d.Head), d.Requests, plural(d.Requests, "request", "requests"))
+}
+
+// Text is the digest a person reads. Four sections with their counts, one line
+// per artefact, and the footer.
+//
+// No line here opens a code fence. A title is the one string in the output an
+// attacker writes, and a fence around it would let a title close the fence and
+// take everything after it out of the block (§9.5).
+func (d Digest) Text() string {
+	var b strings.Builder
+	for _, section := range d.Sections {
+		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "%s (%d)\n", section.Name, section.Count)
+		for _, item := range section.Items {
+			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "  %s\n", item.line())
+		}
+		b.WriteString("\n")
+	}
+	b.WriteString(d.Footer())
+	b.WriteString(d.tail(""))
+	return strings.TrimRight(b.String(), "\n")
+}
+
+// Markdown is `--markdown`. It costs the same requests as every other rendering
+// (§9.7) because it is the same digest, rendered again.
+func (d Digest) Markdown() string {
+	var b strings.Builder
+	for _, section := range d.Sections {
+		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "## %s (%d)\n\n", section.Name, section.Count)
+		for _, item := range section.Items {
+			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- %s\n", item.line())
+		}
+		if len(section.Items) > 0 {
+			b.WriteString("\n")
+		}
+	}
+	b.WriteString(d.Footer())
+	b.WriteString(d.tail("- "))
+	return strings.TrimRight(b.String(), "\n")
+}
+
+// tail is what follows §9.6's footer: the incomplete-answer lines, and
+// `--explain-drops`. Both go after the footer rather than into it, because the
+// footer's shape is fixed by §9.6 and a reader diffing two digests should not
+// have to parse a variable line to find it.
+func (d Digest) tail(bullet string) string {
+	var b strings.Builder
+	for _, shortfall := range d.Incomplete {
+		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "\nincomplete: %s", shortfall)
+	}
+	if len(d.Drops) > 0 {
+		b.WriteString("\n\nnot matched, with the predicates that were evaluated and returned false:\n")
+		for _, drop := range d.Drops {
+			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "%s#%d · %s · %s\n", bullet, drop.Number, strings.Join(drop.Predicates, ", "), drop.URL)
+		}
+	}
+	return b.String()
+}
+
+// line is §9.3's rendering: an identifier, the title, the author, the state the
+// platform computed, and the URL that stands in for everything dropped.
+//
+// The example in §9.3 writes no author. §9.5 requires one — "titles and author
+// logins ... *are* rendered, because an identifier is useless without them" — so
+// it is here, escaped like the title, and the example is read as an illustration
+// of which *kinds* of field survive rather than as the field list.
+func (i Item) line() string {
+	parts := []string{fmt.Sprintf("#%d", i.Number), i.Title}
+	if i.Author != "" {
+		// An artefact whose author the API returned as null — a deleted account —
+		// has no login to print, and inventing one would be the digest asserting
+		// something the platform does not tell it (§9.5).
+		parts = append(parts, "@"+i.Author)
+	}
+	return strings.Join(append(parts, i.State, i.URL), " · ")
+}
